content.value_statement: Event-sourced systems need fast query models that stay aligned with streams. This skill provides projection patterns, templates, and verification guidance for read-side design.
actual_capabilities: Explains live, catchup, persistent, and inline projection types.
Provides templates for basic projectors and order summary read models.
Shows search projection patterns for Elasticsearch-backed query views.
Covers aggregation and multi-table projection examples.
Lists best practices for idempotency, checkpointing, monitoring, and rebuilds.
limitations: It provides patterns and examples, not a complete production framework.
It does not verify database schemas or event contracts automatically.
It does not replace performance testing with real event volume.
It focuses on projection design, not full event store implementation.

use_cases.title: Design a CQRS read side
use_cases.description: Plan tables, handlers, and checkpoints for an event-sourced service.

use_cases.title: Rebuild materialized views
use_cases.description: Choose catchup and persistent projection patterns for historical event replay.

use_cases.title: Improve query performance
use_cases.description: Model search indexes and summaries that avoid expensive stream scans.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic projection
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a simple projection for these event types: [events]. Include the read model fields and update rules.

prompt_templates.title: Plan checkpointing
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a checkpoint strategy for a projection that processes [volume] events and must recover after failures.

prompt_templates.title: Compare projection types
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare live, catchup, persistent, and inline projections for this workflow: [workflow]. Recommend one option with tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Design multi-table projections
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-table projection for [domain]. Include event handlers, consistency concerns, rebuild steps, and monitoring signals.

output_examples.input: Design an order summary projection from order lifecycle events.
output_examples.output: A read model with order status, item count, total amount, timestamps, event handlers, and checkpoint guidance.

output_examples.input: Choose a projection type for rebuilding customer analytics.
output_examples.output: A catchup projection with persistent checkpoints, replay controls, progress metrics, and validation against source events.

output_examples.input: Create a search projection for product catalog events.
output_examples.output: An index design with searchable fields, event-to-document mapping, update rules, and rebuild recommendations.

best_practices: Define idempotent handlers so replayed events do not corrupt read models.
Track checkpoints and lag metrics for every persistent projection.
Plan rebuild procedures before changing projection schemas.
anti_patterns: Do not query event streams directly for high-traffic read paths.
Do not mix write-side validation rules into projection handlers.
Do not deploy projections without replay and recovery checks.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps design read models and projections for CQRS and event-sourced systems.

faq.question: Does it generate production code?
faq.answer: It provides implementation templates and guidance, but users must adapt code to their stack.

faq.question: Can it help with Elasticsearch projections?
faq.answer: Yes. The playbook includes a search projection template for indexing event-derived documents.

faq.question: Does it support projection rebuilds?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains catchup projections, persistent checkpoints, and rebuild-focused practices.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation-based and references only a local playbook file.
